# pvescheduler_placement_fixed (Resource)

Pins VM placement to one explicitly named Proxmox node. The node must exist in the cluster when the resource is created. Changing `node_name` replaces the resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# pvescheduler_placement_fixed pins a VM to one explicitly named node. No
# scoring happens; the node only has to exist in the cluster at creation time.
# Changing node_name replaces the resource.
resource "pvescheduler_placement_fixed" "placement" {
  node_name = "pve01"
}

# Feed the decision into your VM resource, for example:
#
#   node_name = pvescheduler_placement_fixed.placement.node_name
#
output "pinned_node" {
  value = pvescheduler_placement_fixed.placement.node_name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `node_name` (String) The Proxmox node to place the VM on. Changing this forces a new placement.

### Read-Only

- `cpu_usage_pct` (Number) CPU utilization of the node at time of placement, as a percentage (0-100).
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `memory_usage_pct` (Number) Memory utilization of the node at time of placement, as a percentage (0-100).
- `zone` (String) The zone of `node_name` in the provider topology at time of placement, or null if the node is in no zone or in more than one.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the PVE node name to pin this placement to.
terraform import pvescheduler_placement_fixed.placement pve01
```
